title: Fed Decision in September?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent July PCE data showed headline inflation holding at 3.7% year-over-year and core at 3.3%, above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target and prompting modest hawkish repricing ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC meeting. Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole remarks reinforced a high bar for policy easing while describing financial conditions as accommodative and the labor market as consistent with full employment, keeping a hold in play despite sticky price pressures. With the unemployment rate near 4.2% and job growth moderating, traders weigh incoming August employment and CPI releases against the risk that persistent inflation could prompt a 25-basis-point hike. The near-even split between no change and a modest increase reflects uncertainty over whether recent readings represent a temporary spike or sustained reacceleration.

eventMetadata.context_description: JD Vance leads the 2028 presidential winner market at 24.4% as the sitting vice president and early Republican primary frontrunner in multiple polls, benefiting from name recognition and positioning within the party ahead of the first post-Trump cycle. Marco Rubio follows at 10.7% amid his role as secretary of state and consistent second-place polling, while Democratic contenders remain fragmented, with Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez at 11.6% and Jon Ossoff at 11.3% reflecting trader emphasis on visibility over settled polling. Gavin Newsom and Kamala Harris trail further as the broad field awaits post-midterm declarations, endorsements, and primary positioning that could consolidate support.
